notes: Inspire mode: what each craft watches for, and exercise patterns to turn watching into making. Write the actual notes for each film yourself, about that film; these are prompts, not copy.

roles.name: Writer
watch_for: Where the scene starts and ends (late in, early out)
What characters want versus what they say (subtext)
Information held back from the audience, and when it is released
Silence and action doing the work of dialogue
Structure: turning points, the midpoint, how the ending answers the opening
Specific, surprising detail that makes a character real
exercises: Rewrite the key scene with no dialogue at all
Write the scene from the other character's point of view
Cut every line that explains a feeling; keep only actions
Write the conversation that happens off screen just before this scene
Describe a person you know only through objects they own

roles.name: Cinematographer
watch_for: Where the key light comes from, and how hard or soft it is
Lens choice: wide and close, or long and far; what it does to space
When the camera moves, and when it refuses to
Colour: a palette held across the film, and the moment it breaks
Composition: negative space, frames within frames, the horizon line
How night, practicals and motivated light are handled
exercises: Light one corner of your room the way the key scene is lit; shoot it on your phone
Recreate one frame with the lenses you own and compare
Shoot the same action twice: once locked off, once handheld; note what each says
Make a 5-colour palette from the film and dress a small scene in it
Film 60 seconds using only one light source

roles.name: Director
watch_for: Blocking: how people move in the space and what that reveals
Performance: what the actors are allowed not to show
Tone: how the film holds (or mixes) comedy, tension and tenderness
Rhythm across the whole film: fast and slow passages
Point of view: whose story the camera tells
The one image the film is remembered by
exercises: Block the key scene for two friends in your living room, with no dialogue changes
Storyboard the scene in 6 frames from memory, then compare
Tell the same 30-second moment in one shot and in eight shots
Write a one-page director's statement for the film as if it were yours

roles.name: Editor / sound / design
watch_for: Where the cuts fall: on action, on a look, on a sound
How long a shot is held after you expect the cut
Sound that carries emotion more than the picture (and silence)
Transitions: match cuts, sound bridges, hard cuts to black
Production design: rooms, colours and objects that tell the story
Music: when it enters, and when it is withheld
exercises: Re-cut a 1-minute scene from your own footage two ways: tight, and with held shots
Watch the key scene with sound only, then picture only; write what each tells you
Design a room for a character using three objects and one colour
Replace the score of a scene with silence and room tone; what changes?
